provenance: Operator rule (2026-09-22): OpenRouter may serve FREE models only. The openrouter upstream declares paidModelsAllowed:false, so any model whose price is unknown or non-zero is refused at dispatch (packages/core/src/compatibility.ts) — a config mistake cannot spend money. Every openrouter model id below carries the :free variant and cost 0. Ids, context windows, output ceilings, modalities and zero pricing verified live from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models and a real completion per id on 2026-09-22. Jev (TypeSafe judge) is a separate upstream and unaffected by this rule. Operator rule (2026-09-23): Claude Code and Codex are used through their own subscriptions — Sabi installs hooks into them and never writes a provider base URL, an API key or a model override into either harness, so neither can become per-token spend through Sabi. Guarded by packages/controller/test/hooks.test.ts. Operator rule (2026-09-23): transport fallback is ON. Every configured tier is an OpenRouter `:free` model, and those are served from shared upstream pools that rate-limit the whole pool (`limit_source: upstream_provider_shared_pool` in the provider's own 429 body), so a 429 on one free model is routed to the next serving tier instead of ending the round. Fixed aliases are unaffected by design. Operator addition (2026-09-25): native Gemini via the OpenAI-compatible surface. It is NOT in the policy tiers, so default routing never selects it. It is the one upstream with paidModelsAllowed:true and must be requested by name (`sabi-gemini`). Google publishes RPM/TPM/RPD quotas per PROJECT, not per key, and no per-token price for a Free-tier key, so it cannot be proven free and is not claimed to be. Operator addition (2026-09-25): NVIDIA and Mistral upstreams added. Only models verified with a real completion against this account are listed -- codestral-latest, mistral-code-latest, nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b, nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b, nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning. The remaining NVIDIA catalogue entries return 404 'not found for account' or 410 Gone on this key and are deliberately absent. Both upstreams are metered and carry paidModelsAllowed:true; the openrouter free-only rule is unchanged and still enforced per-upstream. Context windows for the NVIDIA models come from the OpenRouter catalogue because NVIDIA's own /v1/models omits them. Operator correction (2026-09-28): the NVIDIA tiers pointed at the PAID model ids while free variants of the same models sat in the same catalogue -- nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free and nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free are both proven 0/0. All three NVIDIA tiers now use the :free ids and declare cost 0. quotaPool is recorded on every tier because seventeen :free models share ONE daily allowance: a 429 on any of them is a statement about all of them, and a lane that counts models rather than pools looks healthy until it can serve nothing. stealth/space-bunny-alpha is priced 0/0 with no :free suffix, so it is funded outside that pool and survives its exhaustion. It is now the 'independent' tier rather than a debugging alias. openrouter/free is excluded from every tier: it is a router that resolves to whichever free model it likes, so the model that answers is never the one named. Operator addition (2026-09-28): a capacity pool, because the candidate universe was config.models and every pool the operator already had but had not written a row for was invisible. The one that mattered most is capacity the HOST holds: OMP serves space-bunny-alpha through the orchestrator, with no key in secrets.env, so an expired OpenRouter key stranded a machine whose best free model was running the session. executor:'host' is the load-bearing field -- Sabi recommends host capacity and the host applies it. A candidate the caller cannot execute is removed from the chain rather than ranked lower, because an unactionable recommendation converts a recoverable failure into a dead end. Operator decision (2026-09-28): tiers are marked diagnostic so they do not appear in /v1/models. Sabi exists to remove the model-picking decision; a picker carrying gemini, nvidia, mistral and local is a different list, not less of one. The advertised surface is sabi-code plus sabi-cheap, sabi-mid and sabi-strong, the last three as escape hatches for someone who wants to pin. Every diagnostic tier stays routable by name, which is what they are for. New providers and new adapters must default to diagnostic. Operator decision (2026-09-28): Ollama removed from the machine entirely. The local tier went with it. It was the last-resort fallback for the whole config, which made a cold 7B load the thing a healthy turn ended on -- 35s on first request, 1.8s once resident, and past a client timeout in between. The live metered upstreams (gemini, nvidia, mistral) answer in seconds and hold keys that work, so they are the floor now. Costs real money per turn; if that is unacceptable, the answer is a working OpenRouter key, not a local model.

harness.provenance: Command Code catalog ids, efforts and min plans verified 2026-09-18 against `cmd --list-models` and the bundled reference models.md. Used by the in-process mod adapter (harness keeps its own loop, no proxy, no key). This is the Command Code subscription catalog, not OpenRouter — the free-models-only rule above does not apply to it.

host-native.description: Capacity the host harness can serve from its own allowance. OMP reaches space-bunny-alpha through the orchestrator rather than through any key in this file, so Sabi could not see it at all until capacity existed. Sabi does not dial these: it recommends them and the host applies the decision.
